endorsements.quote: To build a resilient clinical MVP, developers must move away from interruptive pop-ups and engineer "friction-by-design" for critical interventions, ensuring clinicians remain active cognitive participants.
This step-by-step declaration must include a timestamp, the underlying data points used, and the authorizing clinician's signature.

Therefore, we argue that clinical AI must be evaluated not only by its retrospective predictive accuracy, but by its practical ability to improve workflow, reduce documentation burdens, and support clinician judgment.
To navigate this, emerging policy frameworks must explicitly classify clinical AI software as "high-risk."

Hospitals must treat silent deployments under the same ethical frameworks as clinical trials, utilizing them for operational metrics rather than high-acuity diagnostics, backed by legally binding data-processing agreements that prevent vendors from using ward data to train external commercial models.

This continuous audit trail does more than establish liability; it serves as a critical surveillance mechanism to detect algorithmic drift, clearly indicating to developers and administrators exactly when an underlying AI model requires retraining.
To transition from theoretical implementation to measurable success, hospitals deploying clinical AI must establish rigorous baseline metrics.

unlisted_practices: Mandate that every AI-generated output in the EHR be visibly watermarked.
Deploy AI as a defensive layer that intercepts and queries potential data entry errors before they reach the predictive layer.
Defer non-critical AI insights until the clinician opens the relevant patient's chart rather than interrupting active work.
Use legally binding data-processing agreements to prevent vendors from using ward data to train external commercial models.
Address upstream workflow errors with workflow-level corrective systems before deploying advanced automation.

screen.reason: This is an editorial presenting a conceptual synthesis and recommendations for workflow integration, governance, and safeguards (such as EHR watermarking and audit trails) for clinical AI.
